summary: Rotate an n x n matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place.
mainInsight: A 90-degree clockwise rotation can be done ring by ring: rotate four cells at a time (top -> right -> bottom -> left -> top). The equivalent two-step trick is transpose then reverse each row.

approaches.name: Transpose then reverse each row
approaches.summary: Swap across the diagonal, then reverse rows.

approaches.name: Rotate four cells per step by rings

personalSolution.approach: Rotate four cells per step by rings
personalSolution.notes: Optimal; transpose + reverse is easier to remember.

promptVariants: Which two-step operation rotates a matrix 90 degrees clockwise?
What does transposing then reversing rows do?
options: Reverse each row, then reverse each column
cards.explanation: Transpose turns rows into columns; reversing each row then mirrors horizontally, giving a clockwise rotation.

promptVariants: What is the index mapping of a clockwise rotation?
Why can four cells be rotated together?
cards.answer: Cell (r, c) moves to (c, n - 1 - r). Applying this mapping four times returns to the start, so the cells form cycles of length 4; rotating each 4-cycle in place (top -> right -> bottom -> left) rotates the whole matrix without extra space.
cards.explanation: Layers: i from 0 to n//2, j from i to n-i-2.
Each of the n^2 cells is moved once.
In-place swaps with a few temporaries.

promptVariants: Why does the outer loop run `n // 2` times and the inner loop from i to n - i - 1?
What happens to the centre cell when n is odd?
cards.answer: There are n // 2 concentric layers; layer i has n - 2i cells per side, and rotating a layer needs only the first n - 2i - 1 cells of each side (the last cell of each side is the first cell of the next side, so it is moved as part of another 4-cycle). For odd n the centre cell stays in place and needs no move.
keyPoints: Side length minus one per layer
cards.explanation: A transpose + reverse solution avoids this arithmetic.

cards.answer: Nothing (no layers); one layer plus a fixed centre
cards.explanation: n // 2 = 0 layers for 1x1 and 1 layer for 3x3 (the centre stays).
